PIPELINE (raster path, core/converter.py:convert_image_to_3d L509-1590 -> core/image_processing.py:LuminaImageProcessor):
1. LUT load (image_processing.py:_load_lut L218-487). A LUT .npy is ONLY measured RGB (uint8), shape (32,32,3)=1024 4-color, (36,36,3)=1296 6-color, (74,37,3)=2738 8-color, (6,6,3) with first 32 used = BW, (2468,3)=5-Color Extended; reshape(-1,3) gives lut_rgb (N,3). The "recipe" for row i is reconstructed procedurally, never stored in .npy: 4-color/BW -> base-4/base-2 digits of i, most-significant digit first (L448-458: `stack = digits[::-1]`, so idx1=[0,0,0,0,1], idx256=[1,0,0,0,0]); 6-color -> calibration.get_top_1296_colors() (calibration.py:204-298, greedy selection over 6^5 simulated Lab colors using SmartConfig td alpha-blend) then reversed (L327); 8-color -> assets/smart_8color_stacks.npy (2738,5) uint8 0..7 (first 8 rows are pure [i]*5), reversed (L302); 5-Color Extended -> 1024 base stacks padded with -1 (air) at index 0 + calibration.select_extended_1444_colors() 6-layer stacks (L374-399). .npz merged LUTs store both rgb (N,3) uint8 and stacks (N,5) int32 in the unified 8-color slot space (lut_merger.py:_REMAP_TO_8COLOR L81-88) and are loaded directly (L231-250). Result: self.lut_rgb (N,3) uint8, self.ref_stacks (N, L) int with L = self.layer_count (5, or 6 for 5-Color Extended), self.lut_lab = OpenCV Lab (L 0-255, a/b 0-255 centered at 128) via cv2.COLOR_BGR2Lab (L44-62), self.kdtree = scipy KDTree over lut_lab (L479-480). Row-index <-> physical board cell: extractor.py:run_extraction L245-276 samples row r, col c -> extracted[r,c]; flattening gives i = r*grid+c, which equals the stack index used by calibration.generate_calibration_board L122-136 (block i at row i//32, col i%32, full_matrix[z]=stack[z]). LUT is therefore indexed by ROW ORDINAL, mapping stack -> measured RGB.
2. RECIPE/STACK CONVENTION: ref_stacks[i] is an ordered sequence of filament slot IDs, FIXED length 5 (6 in 5-Color Extended), index 0 = viewing surface (outermost), index L-1 = adjacent to backing (image_processing.py L300-303, color_recipe_logger.py L142-149, converter.py L2245-2250). Slot IDs are per-mode (config.py ColorSystem: RYBW {0 White,1 Red,2 Yellow,3 Blue}; CMYW {0 W,1 C,2 M,3 Y}; SIX_COLOR {0 W,1 C,2 M,3 Green,4 Y,5 K}; EIGHT_COLOR {0 W,1 C,2 M,3 Y,4 K,5 Red,6 DeepBlue,7 Green}; FIVE_COLOR_EXTENDED {0 W,1 R,2 Y,3 B,4 K}, layer_count 6). All calibration measurements are over a WHITE backing (calibration.py:223, 759) and every layer is opaque-filled (no air except -1 in 5C-Ext).
3. Image -> pixels (process_image L489-651): load RGBA, HiFi resolution = 10 px/mm (pixel_scale 0.1 mm), Pixel mode = 1 px per NOZZLE_WIDTH 0.42 mm; NEAREST resize (L591); alpha<10 -> transparent. HiFi (_process_high_fidelity_mode L654-870): bilateralFilter d=9 sigmaColor=sigmaSpace=smooth_sigma (default 10) -> optional medianBlur(blur_kernel) -> cv2.kmeans K-Means++ to quantize_colors (UI default 48, API default 48, function default 32; pre-downscale if >500k px) -> medianBlur(3) -> np.unique colors -> match each unique color -> vectorized map to all pixels via integer code R*65536+G*256+B + searchsorted (L809-828) -> matched_rgb = lut_rgb[idx].reshape(H,W,3), material_matrix = ref_stacks[idx].reshape(H,W,L) (L831-834). Pixel mode: per-pixel direct match (L872-895). Then isolated_pixel_cleanup (HiFi only, enable_cleanup default True; L614-621), then material_matrix[transparent] = -1, mask_solid = ~transparent (L631-632). Output shapes: matched_rgb (H,W,3) uint8, material_matrix (H,W,L) int, mask_solid (H,W) bool.
4. MATCHING: default hue_weight=0 -> pure nearest neighbour in OpenCV-Lab Euclidean (note L axis is 0-255 i.e. scaled x2.55 vs true L*, so this is not exact dE76). hue_weight>0 -> HueAwareColorMatcher (color_matching_hue_aware.py): KDTree prefilter k=32 candidates (image_processing passes k=32, L796/L883), then rerank by sqrt((dL/w_L)^2+(dC/w_C)^2+(dH/w_H)^2) in LCH derived from OpenCV Lab (L102-118), dH = 2*min(C1,C2)*sin(dh/2) (L121-136), w_L=w_C=1, w_H=0.15+0.85*(1-hw)^3 (L97-100). With hue matcher, a post-match pass does medianBlur(5) then (3) on matched_rgb and RE-MATCHES via plain KDTree (L840-854). NO DITHERING anywhere in the repo (grep dither/floyd/error-diffusion: zero hits); matching is hard nearest-neighbour per unique colour, so smooth gradients become posterised bands of LUT colours.
5. CLEANUP (isolated_pixel_cleanup.py L135-210): encodes each pixel's L-layer stack as one int (base = max_id+1), flags pixels whose code differs from all 8 neighbours, replaces with neighbourhood mode code and looks up lut_rgb/ref_stacks by code (dict encode->lut idx, L179-186). Requires ref_stacks and lut_rgb aligned.
6. Post-processing hooks: color_replacements / replacement_regions (converter.py L905-944) re-query kdtree for the replacement RGB and overwrite material_matrix[mask] = ref_stacks[idx]; ColorMerger (color_merger.py) merges low-usage palette colours in Lab dE76 (used by UI preview flow); ColorRecipeLogger writes per-colour stack recipe report (converter.py L1482-1494).
7. VOXELISATION (converter.py:_build_voxel_matrix L2150-2212, default path L1074-1078): full_matrix (Z,H,W) int, -1 = air. bottom_voxels = transpose(material_matrix,(2,0,1)) so full_matrix[z] = material_matrix[:,:,z] for z in 0..L-1 -> STACK INDEX 0 (VIEWING SURFACE) IS PRINTED AT Z=0 ON THE BED (face-down print); then spacer_layers = round(spacer_thick/0.08) layers of backing_color_id (default slot 0 = white) over mask_solid; UI default structure "双面"/Double-sided (ui/layout_new.py:2323) appends a mirrored copy (material_matrix[..., ::-1]) on top -> total Z = 2L + spacer. Single-sided: Z = L + spacer, then X-mirror at L1401-1411. 5-Color Extended forces single-sided face-up via _build_voxel_matrix_faceup (L2238-2277: viewing index 0 at highest Z, -1 stays air) plus Z flip at L1385-1399. Relief (_build_relief_voxel_matrix L1954-2076) puts the 5 optical layers at the top of a per-pixel/ per-colour height column, face-up.
8. MESHING/EXPORT: one mesh per material slot (converter.py L1113-1157, HighFidelityMesher mesh_generators.py:198 does per-Z mask -> 3x3 dilation -> merge identical consecutive Z masks -> greedy rectangles -> boxes; VoxelMesher for pixel mode). Scene -> export_scene_with_bambu_metadata (bambu_3mf_writer.py L676-763): one 3MF object per USED slot in valid_slot_names order; model_settings.config assigns extruder = 1-based object order (L413), filament_colour from preview_colors (L492-500; overridden with LUT-measured pure-stack colours via _get_actual_lut_slot_colors converter.py L466-504), single_extruder_multi_material=1, enable_prime_tower=1, filament_map_mode 'Auto For Flush' (L420, 571-572), layer_height 0.08, wall_loops 1, 0 top/bottom shells, 100% zig-zag infill (converter.py L1437-1453).
9. FILAMENT CHANGES IMPLIED: every optical Z layer is a mosaic of per-pixel materials. Verified: in the 4-color 1024 set every layer position takes all 4 values; in smart_8color_stacks every column has all 8 IDs (unique per column = [8,8,8,8,8]). So per optical layer Bambu needs (distinct materials present in that Z) - 1 changes, i.e. up to 3 (4-color), 5 (6-color), 7 (8-color) per layer, x5 layers, x2 if double-sided, plus one change into/out of the backing colour. Default double-sided 4-colour ~30-40 swaps; 8-colour ~70+. Only existing per-layer material-count constraint: 5-Color Extended keeps "<=4 materials per Z" by structural design (air pad at index 0 for base stacks so the top Z has only R/Y/B/K; converter.py L986-998, L2249-2250, ui/layout_new.py:3432) -- an AMS-4-slot compatibility argument, NOT a global layer order. There is NO option for a HueForge-style global filament-per-layer order anywhere (converter, image_processing, vector_engine _build_channel_runs L458-478 just run-length-encodes each recipe independently).
10. 5-COLOR: two distinct things. (a) core/five_color_combination.py is a QUERY/UI helper (ColorQueryEngine.query: find row where stack_lut == [5 indices] -> lut_rgb[row]; KNOWN_FORMATS 1024->4, 2468->5, 1296->6, 2738->8; validates stack shape (N,5) and values 0..7). It does not participate in conversion. (b) "5-Color Extended" mode (config FIVE_COLOR_EXTENDED, layer_count 6, ID 4 = Black) = 1024 RYBW 5-layer stacks padded with -1 + 1444 six-layer stacks with a single outer layer R/Y/B (or the special KWWWWW) chosen greedily by simulated RGB distance >8 (calibration.py L737-852); LUT 2468 rows; forced single-sided face-up; incompatible with relief. Difference from 4/6/8: 6-layer stacks with air, viewing surface at top, and the Z-flip/mirror special-casing in converter L1385-1423.
11. WHERE TO IMPOSE A GLOBAL LAYER ORDER (same filament for the whole Z layer): the correct place is the candidate set, i.e. filter (lut_rgb, ref_stacks) BEFORE the KDTree is built in LuminaImageProcessor._load_lut -- insert immediately before core/image_processing.py:479 (`self.lut_lab = self._rgb_to_lab(self.lut_rgb)`) and also before the early returns at L238-239 and L360-361 (npz paths), or as a new method called right after `self._load_lut(lut_path)` in __init__ (L87) that rebuilds lut_lab/kdtree/hue_matcher. Keep only rows whose ref_stacks[i][z] is in allowed_set[z] for every z (strict HueForge-style: allowed_set[z] = {order[z]} which for a fixed 5-layer, no-air model collapses to one stack -> you must instead allow per-pixel variable HEIGHT, i.e. reuse _build_relief_voxel_matrix at converter.py:1954 and replace the per-pixel material fill at L2036-2043 / L2056-2060 with full_matrix[z][mask_solid & (z < height_z)] = global_order[z], choosing height per pixel by nearest simulated colour of prefix stacks -- there is no measured LUT for such stacks, only the TD alpha-blend simulator at calibration.py L225-240 / L769-781). A cheaper middle ground that keeps the measured LUT: allowed_set[z] = {order[z], white} (<=2 materials per layer -> 1 swap per layer) applied at the same L479 filter point. Everything downstream (cleanup, recipe logger, voxel build, mesher, 3MF) already tolerates an arbitrary subset of stacks; only _get_actual_lut_slot_colors (converter.py:466) needs pure stacks to derive AMS colours, falling back to ColorSystem preview colours otherwise. To emit only 5 filaments from the user's 12, define a 5-slot ColorSystem entry (config.py) so num_materials/slot_names (converter.py L835-840, L1114) match, and note the 3MF extruder index follows valid_slot_names order (unused slots are dropped, bambu_3mf_writer.py L406-413).

risks: All measured LUTs assume a WHITE backing and fully opaque 5-layer fills; a custom 5-filament palette from the user's 12 spools has NO measured LUT -- either print/photograph a calibration board (calibration.generate_calibration_board / extractor.run_extraction) or fall back to the TD alpha-blend simulator, whose td values are per-filament guesses (SmartConfig.FILAMENTS, calibration.py:761-767)

Stack convention is inconsistent on disk vs in memory: assets/smart_8color_stacks.npy and get_top_1296_colors are bottom-to-top and reversed at load; .npz merged files are already top-to-bottom; 4-colour base-4 digits are MSB=viewing. Any new LUT must follow 'index 0 = viewing surface' or colours will be inverted

Default voxel build is FACE-DOWN (viewing surface at Z=0 on the bed) and the UI default is double-sided; HueForge references are face-up with a heightmap. Face-up in this repo exists only for 5-Color Extended, relief and cloisonne paths (converter.py:986-1078), each with special Z-flip/X-mirror handling (L1385-1423) that must be replicated

Enforcing a strict one-filament-per-Z order on the fixed 5-layer no-air model collapses the LUT to a single stack; you need per-pixel variable height (relief path) or a relaxed constraint (e.g. {order[z], white} per layer) to keep >1 colour

Filtering ref_stacks/lut_rgb may remove the pure stacks that _get_actual_lut_slot_colors (converter.py:466) uses to set AMS colours; then preview colours fall back to hard-coded ColorSystem values (CMYW/RYBW defaults) and Bambu Studio will show wrong filament colours

3MF extruder numbering follows valid_slot_names order with unused slots dropped (bambu_3mf_writer.py:406-413), so filament N in Bambu Studio != material ID N when a slot has no geometry; also filament_settings_id is hard-coded 'Bambu PLA Basic @BBL H2D' (L503) and 8 nozzle temps (converter.py:1445-1447)

No dithering: nearest-neighbour matching on K-Means-quantised colours produces posterised bands; HueForge-quality gradients require adding error-diffusion or per-pixel height gradation, neither present

Matching is in OpenCV-scaled Lab (L x2.55), not true dE76/dE2000, so luminance is over-weighted relative to chroma; hue_weight>0 mitigates but then a medianBlur+re-match pass (image_processing.py:840-854) partially undoes hue protection

HighFidelityMesher dilates every material mask by 1 px (0.1 mm) per Z (mesh_generators.py:403-407) -> overlapping objects between materials; Bambu resolves overlaps by object order, which may bias which filament wins at boundaries

4-colour LUT load silently drops 'outlier' rows (image_processing.py:444-466), so lut_rgb row index no longer equals the base-4 code; never derive stacks from row index after load -- always use ref_stacks
converter.py:957 KeyError (mode_info['name']) means HiFi debug previews are never saved; harmless but hides quantisation output

5-Color Extended LUT loading from .npy regenerates 1444 stacks via greedy selection at every load (calibration.py:737-852); if the simulator constants change, stack<->row alignment with a previously photographed board breaks

1) 3MF TOPOLOGY. The writer (utils/bambu_3mf_writer.py, class BambuStudio3MFWriter) emits ONE OBJECT PER FILAMENT SLOT, not per layer, no painted triangles (no mmu_segmentation/paint_color attributes), no per-layer custom gcode (Metadata/custom_gcode_per_layer.xml is never written; filament_sequence.json is {"plate_1":{"sequence":[]}}). No thumbnail, no plate png, no G-code, no transforms/UUIDs; Bambu Studio auto-centers. Header claims Application=BambuStudio-02.04.00.70.

2) HOW FILAMENT ASSIGNMENT IS ENCODED. model_settings.config: <object id=N+1> containing <part id=k subtype="normal_part"> with <metadata key="name" value=slot_name/> and <metadata key="extruder" value=str(k)/> — part index k == filament index k (1-based), hard-wired (writer line 413). <plate> has plater_id=1, filament_map_mode="Auto For Flush", one model_instance. project_settings.config: filament_colour / filament_multi_colour / default_filament_colour are built from the RGB of each added mesh in add order (lines 492-500); every key starting with "filament_" plus the temperature/fan/plate-temp keys listed at lines 549-560 are resized to num_colors=len(self.objects) by copying element 0 (lines 546-565); then _build_filament_arrays overrides with hard constants (Bambu PLA Basic @BBL H2D, GFA00, 220C nozzle, 60C bed, flow 1, max vol speed 15, filament_map all '1'). single_extruder_multi_material='1', enable_prime_tower='1' forced (571-572). Bambu Studio therefore shows N filaments with those hex colours, one part per filament, and performs a tool change every time a layer contains >1 part material.

3) CAN IT TAKE 5+ FILAMENTS? Yes mechanically: num_colors is simply the number of meshes added; there is no 4/8 cap anywhere in the writer. Caveats: (a) export_scene_with_bambu_metadata maps names→colours via ColorSystem.get(color_mode)['slots'] with substring matching (line 730); unknown names fall to gray (200,200,200), so a custom 5-colour mode needs a ColorSystem entry (config.py:131-268) with 'slots','preview','map' and the mode string must not be swallowed by the substring checks in ColorSystem.get (e.g. "4-Color", "6-Color", "BW"). (b) In the raster path preview colours are overridden from the LUT's pure stacks (converter.py:883-892, _get_actual_lut_slot_colors at 466-504) so filament_colour reflects measured calibration colour, not the nominal hex. (c) flush_volumes_matrix (32 entries = 2 extruders × 4×4, template) is NOT resized (key lacks 'filament_' prefix) — for N=5 Bambu expects 2×25; filament_self_index is resized to all '1' (should be 1..N); filament_map all '1' (everything on H2D extruder 1). (d) Only parts that produced non-empty meshes are exported (converter.py:1140-1158), and extruder ids are renumbered 1..M by position — an unused slot shifts all following AMS slots. (e) Every extra mesh (Backing, Keychain_Loop, Outline, Coating, Wire, Free_xxx) becomes an ADDITIONAL filament index because extruder=idx; "Backing" gets gray (no name match), only "Board" (vector path) maps to slot 0 colour.

4) PHYSICAL STRUCTURE (raster/HiFi default). PrinterConfig (config.py:57-63): LAYER_HEIGHT=0.08, NOZZLE_WIDTH=0.42, COLOR_LAYERS=5, BACKING_MM=1.6 (unused by UI; UI slider default 1.2, range 0.2–3.5 step 0.08 at ui/layout_new.py:2231-2234). Resolution: HiFi 10 px/mm → pixel_scale 0.1 mm (image_processing.py:566-571); Pixel mode 1 px = 0.42 mm (574-575); rasterised SVG 20 px/mm = 0.05 (541). target_w=int(width_mm*10), target_h scaled by aspect; width slider default 60 mm (10–400). material_matrix (H,W,L) from ref_stacks (image_processing.py:832, 889), L=layer_count (5 for 4/6/8-colour, 6 for 5-Color Extended), values slot id or -1; index 0 = viewing surface (top-to-bottom convention, converter.py:470,487). _build_voxel_matrix (converter.py:2150-2212): Z 0..L-1 = optical layers (viewing surface at Z=0 = FIRST printed layer, face-down print), Z L..L+spacer-1 = backing_color_id (default 0=White, so backing voxels are inside the White mesh; -2 when separate_backing) on mask_solid; spacer_layers=round(spacer/0.08). Total height = 0.4 + spacer (default 1.2 → 20 layers = 1.6 mm; verified bbox z 0→1.60). Double-sided adds L reversed optical layers on top (0.4+spacer+0.4). Relief (1954-2076): OPTICAL_LAYERS hard-coded 5, base below to per-pixel/colour height. Face-up variants (5-Color Extended, 2238-2277; vector face_up) put backing at Z=0. Single-sided output is X-mirrored about model width (converter.py:1401-1411) so the print reads correctly after flipping.

5) MESHING (core/mesh_generators.py). HighFidelityMesher.generate_mesh(voxel,mat_id,height_px): per Z mask==mat_id → cv2.dilate 3×3 one iteration (+1 px each side = +0.1 mm in HiFi, so adjacent materials OVERLAP by 1 px; lines 388-407) → group consecutive identical Z masks (378-422) → greedy maximal rectangles (numba or vectorised; 300-376) → one 8-vert/12-tri box per rect per group, y flipped (world_y = height_px - y), Z in layer units → trimesh merge_vertices + unique_faces → scaled by diag(pixel_scale,pixel_scale,0.08) in converter.py:1103-1106. VoxelMesher (pixel art) shrinks each run box by 0.05 px for gaps. Real 200 mm HiFi 4C output: 4 objects with 1.87M/2.27M/2.55M/2.81M triangles (≈9.5M total, 728 MB XML, 74 MB 3mf). Vector path (core/vector_engine.py): SVG shapes → occlusion clip → LUT recipe per fill → run-length extrusion per channel (consecutive same-channel layers merged, 457-529) → backing silhouette extruded at z=num_layers*0.08 merged into slot 0 "White" unless separate_backing ("Board"); one geometry per slot sorted by mat_id (261-283).

6) FILAMENT-CHANGE COST. Print sequence is 'by layer'; in each of the 5 optical layers up to N materials appear → up to (N-1) changes/layer, ≈5(N-1)+1 changes for a 20-layer plaque, plus flush at each (filament_prime_volume 30, minimal purge 15, prime_tower_width '230', wipe tower at 80,250, flush_into_infill/objects '0', flush_into_support '1' — all straight from bambu_config_template.json which is an H2D "版画" process; printer_model/printer_settings_id/printable_area/extruder_* are all H2D-specific and would need to be re-exported from an X2D project). Output-level levers: (i) constrain the voxel matrix so each Z has ≤1 (HueForge-style) or ≤2 materials → changes = number of Z transitions where filament set changes; the writer needs no change because parts are per-filament; (ii) allow several parts to share one extruder value (modify _write_model_settings so extruder comes from a name→filament map instead of idx) to stop Backing/Outline/Loop becoming extra filaments; (iii) emit Metadata/custom_gcode_per_layer.xml (<custom_gcodes_per_layer><plate><plate_info id="1"/><layer top_z=… type="2" extruder=… color=…/>…<mode value="MultiAsSingle"/></plate>) with a single-material mesh for true HueForge parity — not implemented anywhere; (iv) lower purge cost via filament_prime_volume, flush_volumes_matrix (per-pair), flush_into_infill/objects='1', smaller prime_tower_width; (v) backing layers are already single-material (no changes) so thicker backing does not add changes.

HighFidelityMesher dilates each material by one pixel (0.1 mm at 10 px/mm), so parts overlap by 0.1 mm; Bambu resolves overlapping parts by part order (later part wins), so filament order in slot_names affects which colour prints at boundaries

summary:
LUT = a calibration lookup table of MEASURED sRGB values indexed by layer-stack recipe. It carries no metadata (no filament names, hex, TD, brand, order); everything else is inferred from array size + filename keywords + a deterministic index→stack rule.

PHYSICAL FORMAT (.npy, all uint8 RGB, verified with numpy on every file in lut-npy预设/):
- BW: (6,6,3) = 36 cells, only first 32 valid (rows 32-35 are [0,0,0] filler). Index i ∈ 0..31, base-2 digits → stack.
- 4-Color (RYBW or CMYW): (32,32,3) = 1024. Index i base-4, 5 digits, stack = digits[::-1] (MSB = stack[0] = VIEWING surface). Pure stack (i,i,i,i,i) sits at index i*341. Slot ids: RYBW 0=White,1=Red,2=Yellow,3=Blue; CMYW 0=White,1=Cyan,2=Magenta,3=Yellow (config.py:134-160).
- 6-Color (CMYWGK or RYBWGK): (36,36,3) = 1296. Index i ↔ get_top_1296_colors()[i] (core/calibration.py:204-298), a greedy simulated selection of 1296 out of 6^5=7776 (seeds = 6 pure stacks at idx 0-5, then RGB-distance>8 greedy, then fill). Returned bottom-to-top and reversed at every load (image_processing.py:324-327). Slot ids 0=White,1=Cyan/Red,2=Magenta/Blue,3=Green,4=Yellow,5=Black.
- 8-Color: (74,37,3) = 2738 = two 37x37 pages (1369 each) concatenated on axis 0 (ui/callbacks.py:728). Index i ↔ assets/smart_8color_stacks.npy (2738,5) uint8, values 0..7, stored bottom-to-top, reversed at load (image_processing.py:296-302). Rows 0-7 are pure stacks. Generator script analyze_colors.py is referenced (calibration.py:465) but NOT in repo. Slots 0=White,1=Cyan,2=Magenta,3=Yellow,4=Black,5=Red,6=DeepBlue,7=Green.
- 5-Color Extended: (2468,3) = vstack(page1 (32,32,3)→1024, page2 (38,38,3)→1444) (callbacks.py:768-773). Index 0..1023 = 4-color RYBW base stacks padded to 6 layers with -1 (air) at stack[0]; 1024..2467 = select_extended_1444_colors(base) (calibration.py:737-852): 6-layer stacks, viewing layer ∈ {R,Y,B} plus special KWWWWW first; greedy RGB-dist>8. Slots 0=W,1=R,2=Y,3=B,4=K. Only one preset exists: Aliz/PETG/Aliz&PETG&5color&红-黄-蓝-白-黑-20260304.npy. Forces single-sided face-up (≤4 materials per Z) and disables relief (converter.py:988-999, layout_new.py:3431-3440).
- Merged (.npz): keys 'rgb' (N,3) uint8 and 'stacks' (N,5) int32 (or (N,6) for 5C-EXT), stacks in unified 8-color ids, top-to-bottom. Loader accepts ANY N with no validation (image_processing.py:231-250). Remap tables lut_merger.py:81-88.

HOW A PRESET DEFINES COLORS/ORDER: it does not. Order is fixed by mode slot table (config.ColorSystem) + filename keyword (RYBW/CMYW; 6-color default CMYWGK when no keyword — naming convention .md lines 37-79, lut_merger.py:91-112). Actual filament display colours written into the 3MF are derived at convert time from the LUT's pure-stack entries: converter._get_actual_lut_slot_colors (converter.py:466-504) finds rows where all layers == slot_id and overrides preview_colors (converter.py:883-892). bambu_3mf_writer._build_filament_arrays (utils/bambu_3mf_writer.py:477-528) emits filament_colour from mesh order and hardcodes filament_settings_id='Bambu PLA Basic @BBL H2D', vendor 'Bambu Lab', ids 'GFA00', 220/60°C for every slot.

(2) Print, photograph. (3) extractor.run_extraction (core/extractor.py:163-287): click 4 corners → perspective warp to 1000x1000 → optional auto white balance from 50 px corner patches (133-140) and vignette correction in Lab (143-160) → mean of 8x8 px at each cell centre with offset/zoom/barrel knobs → save (grid,grid,3) uint8 to output/lumina_lut.npy (config.py:289). No ICC/colour management; the LUT is camera+lighting dependent.

SYNTHETIC LUT: there is NO code path that produces lut_rgb from hex+TD. The only optical model is naive alpha compositing used solely to CHOOSE which stacks go on a board: alpha = min(1, 0.08/(td/10)); curr = rgb*alpha + curr*(1-alpha) iterated over white backing (calibration.py:226-240, 769-781, 879-893) with hardcoded FILAMENTS (config.py:106-113: W td5.0, C3.5, M3.0, G2.0, Y6.0, K0.6; calibration.py:761-767: W5.0,R4.0,Y6.0,B2.0,K0.6). Black td=0.6 gives alpha=1.0 (fully opaque). Simulated RGB is discarded. README.md:131-134 mentions a 2.0-beta gradient-card + simulation approach but it is not in this repo (v1.6.9). However a synthetic LUT is structurally trivial: any .npz with rgb (N,3) uint8 + stacks (N,L) int32 loads through the Merged branch with color_mode "Merged" (→ EIGHT_COLOR 8-slot config, config.py:257-258); include pure (i,)*L rows so _get_actual_lut_slot_colors can label AMS slots.

risks: No preset matches the user's exact 12 filaments: Bambu presets cover W/C/M/Y/K/Red #C12E1F/Blue #0A2989/Green #00AE42; user's Klein Blue #1E44BE is a different filament from Bambu Blue, and Vivid Yellow #F4E62A ≠ Bambu Yellow #F4EE2A; Coffee Brown, Sunny Orange, Oak, Lavender, Pink, Beige have no LUT at all — any palette using them requires a new calibration print or a synthetic LUT.

Bambulab&PLA&8色-New.npy pure rows (idx 0-7) are exactly nominal hex codes, i.e. hand-edited, so its 'measured' pure colours are not measurements; and Custom/Bambulab&PLA&RYBW&红-黄-蓝-白.npy is byte-identical to the generic 通用LUT and Elegoo file (pure white reads #C3D6E8) — it is not a Bambu calibration despite the name.

There is no model-based LUT generator: the alpha-compositing code only selects board stacks and its optical model is crude (single alpha per filament, no Beer-Lambert, K forced opaque at td 0.6). Building a synthetic LUT from hex+TD is possible via the .npz path but its colour accuracy is unvalidated versus HueForge-grade references.

All LUTs are camera/lighting dependent (auto white balance from corner patches, 8x8 px means, no ICC); LUTs from different photos/brands are not colorimetrically consistent, so merging or subsetting across presets mixes measurement conditions.

6-color and 5C-EXT stacks are recomputed at every load by greedy simulation (get_top_1296_colors / select_extended_1444_colors); any change to the hardcoded FILAMENTS rgb/td or layer height silently changes index→stack mapping and breaks every existing 6C/5C-EXT preset.

Mode detection is size/keyword based: a custom 5-colour LUT of non-standard size falls into 'Merged' (8-slot config, placeholder zero stacks unless .npz); utils/lut_manager.infer_color_mode has no 2468 branch (badges Aliz 5color as 6-Color); files without RYBW/CMYW keyword default to RYBW/CMYWGK (Snapmaker B(蓝)MYW gets wrong slot labels).

Reducing filament changes is not a LUT-level concept in this repo: every stack is 5 (or 6) layers with arbitrary per-layer material, and smart_8color_stacks has 1271 four-material and 339 five-material rows; restricting to few-material stacks shrinks the palette sharply (only 160 two-material and 8 pure rows), so fewer-change output needs new stack selection + new calibration or synthetic data.

risks: Reference meshes are NOT layer-quantized (continuous z, ~11% near-grid); emitting stepped 0.08 columns (Lumina voxel style) changes the slicer's anti-aliasing behaviour: with continuous slopes each layer boundary lands at a sub-pixel position, giving the soft tonal ramps seen in the reference photo; hard quantized steps produce posterized edges as in the user's current file (bimodal distribution, 66% of area in one band).

custom_gcode_per_layer top_z must exactly match a layer top (FL + 0.08*(n-1)) for the configured initial_layer_print_height; the user's file has layer_height 0.2 / initial 0.2 (stale profile), so band boundaries 0.88/1.20/1.68 fall mid-layer and the README's '0.08 preconfigured' claim is false — any new emitter must write layer_height and initial_layer_print_height explicitly and compute top_z from them.

Colour-by-part (user's rebuild3 approach) with stacked slabs works only if slab boundaries are layer-aligned; if a layer's slice plane crosses a slab boundary the layer contains two parts and the slicer inserts a real tool change on that layer (with prime tower enabled => wipe tower every layer). The reference avoids this entirely by using one part + MultiAsSingle plate-wide swaps.

User's project_settings.config has inconsistent filament-array lengths (4 colours vs 3 ids/vendors, 18 temperatures) and a stale plate_1.json for a different album; Bambu Studio may silently reset filaments to defaults or fail to load colours — the emitter must regenerate all per-filament arrays to length n from a single source.

Graduation reference is P1P/Matte with 15% infill and only top_shell 9 (0.72 mm): its surface quality depends on the relief being thinner than the solid top shell; for 2.2 mm relief over a base on the X2D use 100% infill or top_shell_layers >= relief/0.08 (Astroworld uses 9999) to avoid infill show-through in thin light bands.

Reference gcode colours in custom_gcode_per_layer.xml (Graduation #FF0000) do not match filament_colour (#FF00FF): Bambu Studio keys the swap on extruder index, not the color attribute; keep extruder indices 1-based and consistent with filament_colour order.

Astroworld reference is printed at 133.33 mm via a 0.66665 XY build-scale of a 200 mm mesh; pixel pitch (~0.075 mm printed) is well below the 0.42 mm line width — the slicer, not the mesh, sets the effective resolution, so a 450-px grid over 150 mm (0.33 mm) as in the user's file is coarser than the reference and is visible as blockiness in slopes.

The framed reference variants carry a 4.0 mm frame plateau as part of the same heightmap solid (3.8-5.9% of top area) printed in the last colour (white); a frame-less design must still provide a full-height perimeter or the thin 0.72 mm base edge is fragile.

Transmission distances differ per filament (Grad description: Black 0.2, Purple 1.1, Pink 8, White 5 in HueForge units); band thickness in the references (2-8 layers) is tuned to those TDs — reusing 0.88/1.20/1.68 heights with the user's filaments (rebuild3 TD table 0.35-0.7) without recomputing will not reproduce the tonal spacing.
